_what_this_is: the complete enumeration of the six failures that aborted C1 attempt 4 at the pod CPU test gate. All six names came home this time: the FAILED/ERROR grep added after attempt 3R worked, so nothing had to be reconstructed.
died_at: the CPU pytest gate, before TESTS_OK
reconciliation: the pod skipped 49 MORE tests than the sweep and failed 6 that the sweep passed; 49 + 6 = 55 = the pass delta (2798 - 2743). The simulation was exactly 55 tests' worth more generous than the pod.
root_cause: the launch-bound sweep ran with simulate_pod_env.sh's DEFAULT HIDDEN_PATHS instead of a set derived from what THIS session stages. The simulator's own docstring says to pass a session-specific HIDDEN_PATHS -- 'Simulate the session you are about to launch by hiding the initializations it does not stage' -- and its default comment asserts that 'every pod session stages artifacts/stage3/corpus_v2 from the relay', which is FALSE for C1. C1 stages 3 relay dests and 4 local assets, and corpus_v2 is in neither. So the sweep certified a machine more generous than the pod, which is the same class of defect as attempt 3R: a green simulation describing a machine that does not exist. Gate 12 was built to prevent exactly this and did not, because the simulator's fidelity is parameterised by a hand-passed variable I left at its default.

the_six.cause: MY OWN DEFECT, introduced with the gate-12 lineage work. The test calls verify_record(record, REPO) with no authorization_path, so only the readiness record is a permitted post-sweep path. On the pod, HEAD IS the session commit, which by construction also carries logs/autoinit_c1_authorization.json -- so the authorization reads as post-sweep drift and the record is refused.
the_six.reproduced_at_zero_cost: verify_record(r, '.') -> FAIL 'post-sweep drift: 1 path(s) other than [record] changed'; verify_record(r, '.', authorization_path=AUTH) -> PASS.
the_six.note: the GATE is correct -- the launcher passes authorization_path and gate 12 passed. Only the test omits it, so it can never pass on an issued-session tree. It could not have been caught by any pre-issuance sweep, because before issuance the authorization is not in the tree.

the_six.cause: they read artifacts/stage3/corpus_v2/sessions.jsonl and artifacts/eval/battery_v2/manifest.json. C1 stages NEITHER: its relay dests are stage1/e8_calibration_v1, stage1/qwen3_0p6b_init_v0/checkpoint and stage3/ladder_uniform_probe, and its local assets are c1_confirmation_v1, reasoning_heavy_v2, state_eval_v1 and recovery_search_v2. The simulator's default hidden set hides neither, so they passed in the sweep.

they need a host-local retained probe store that no pod has. Phase B's own session ignores this file in SESSION_TEST_IGNORES; C1's ignore list has only test_recovery_corpus_pipeline.py and test_phase_a_stages1_5_execute.py. The file name says hostlocal.

what_worked: every gap closed after earlier attempts stayed closed. All 12 pre-provider gates passed on the launcher's own fresh run; the bundle round-tripped; VLLM_READY, TEACHER_READY and ROPE_OK were all reached; the FAILED/ERROR grep added after 3R brought all six names home with no reconstruction; the watchdog ran independently and ended on pod_gone; teardown was automatic and provider-confirmed.
scientific_result: NONE. C1 has still never been measured.

_correction_20260905._what_this_is: a fresh review found the six-failure enumeration correct but the root-cause SENTENCE too coarse. The six failures below are preserved verbatim; nothing above this key has been rewritten.
_correction_20260905.superseded_claim: 'the root cause is one thing' -- that wording collapsed an escape MECHANISM, three failure CLASSES and a fourth defect that produced no failure at all into a single sentence.

corrected_structure.one_readiness_escape_mechanism: the launch-bound simulator was not mechanically bound to the C1 staging contract. It ran on a hand-maintained complement (HIDDEN_PATHS) instead of a view derived from the session's own SetupManifest, so it could not be checked against the session it claimed to model.
three_actual_pod_failure_classes: the issued-session readiness test omitting authorization_path (1)
battery cases reading historical roles C1 does not stage (2)
the Phase-B host-local module, whose store no pod has (3)
corrected_structure.plus_one_vacuous_pass_that_never_failed: the battery_v2 parameter of test_it_is_disjoint_from_each_jsonl_role_by_id_and_by_content. With the directory absent, load() globbed it to an empty row set and both `not own & role` assertions held TRIVIALLY -- it reported disjointness from a role it had never read, and would have gone on reporting green indefinitely. It is worse than the six, because nothing would ever have surfaced it. The same hole existed in the host-side verifier, which returned 'zero collisions' for an absent role.
